rationale: Provides standardised multi-environment agentic tasks that measure what LLM agents can actually accomplish, directly operationalising evaluation of agent capabilities.
Exercises the production agent attack surface with 160+ adversarial probes, yielding a risk profile of a specific deployed agent rather than of a bare model.
Signed manifests record an asset's edit history including AI-tool edits, giving detectors a provenance basis for distinguishing a genuine image later AI-edited from a wholly synthetic one.
Supplies attribution and activation-level analysis of a model's internals on given data -- the core machinery RQ21 asks about for characterising capabilities and weaknesses.
Machine-readable mapping of AI-lifecycle components to their associated risks and controls is a structured answer to which risks attach to which types of systems.
CTF, self-proliferation, and self-reasoning tasks are agentic evaluations measuring whether a model can autonomously execute risky multi-step behaviour.
Trains and evaluates 15+ detectors under unified cross-dataset protocols -- how detector robustness against evolving generators gets empirically measured.
Fuses an ensemble of image/video/audio detectors behind one API -- an implemented strategy for raising detector robustness beyond any single model's generalisation limits.
Automatically scores whether a dataset carries the metadata needed for it to be findable, licensed and reusable, operationalising what information a dataset must expose before reuse.
Captures and makes queryable the runtime provenance linking a training run to the specific data it consumed, giving an auditable record of whether a model saw a given dataset.
A concrete open specification for the schema, provenance, and licensing metadata that must accompany a dataset -- a candidate reporting requirement.
Defines identity and provenance fields for models/agents/datasets and operates a live registry with an API -- a concrete proposal for the minimum tracked on model updates.
Homomorphic encryption permits computation over encrypted user interaction data so aggregate analysis is possible without exposing individual records.
Gives white-box access to and control over weights and activations -- the substrate for establishing model properties when full model access is available.
A JSON Schema specifying the origin, annotation, and labeler provenance a dataset should report -- directly a candidate metadata reporting requirement for responsible data practice.
A maintained taxonomy enumerating the risk classes that attach to LLM application deployments and how they arise.
Enables model training and analysis on data that never leaves the data owner's server, reconciling third-party data access with privacy-preserving ML.
Its simulated membership-inference machinery is precisely the mechanism for testing whether a model retains signal from specific data, i.e. whether it was trained on it.
Produces differentially private synthetic tabular data that preserves analytic utility, letting third parties work with the data's structure without access to real records.
Control vectors trained from contrastive prompts and applied at inference are a lightweight post-deployment behavioural correction that requires no retraining or redeployment of weights.
Embeds imperceptible video/image watermarks explicitly engineered for robust recovery under transformations -- the defence RQ65 asks about.
Classifies incoming prompts for jailbreak and harm categories at inference time -- the detection step for flagging requests that seek dual-use capability.
Runs workloads in TDX/SEV-SNP VMs with H100 confidential computing and produces remote attestation evidence binding the deployment to specific hardware.
Provides working reference implementations of SGX/TDX remote attestation for real cloud AI workloads, demonstrating what TEEs can attest to in practice.
Gates release of secrets (including model weights or their decryption keys) on TEE attestation evidence -- an infrastructure-level control that denies weights to any unattested host.
